critical_steps: Each unit-vector energy density has total mass 1.
The half-L1 distance equals the supremum over measurable sets of the norm of the difference of the two partial frame operators.
For fixed vector f, measurable selection of the pointwise smaller density minimizes weaving energy and yields 1-TV(f).
Taking joint infimum over vectors and measurable partitions produces 1-tau, and joint supremum produces 1+tau.
A two-point family of positive diagonal local energy operators realizes tau=t and exact weaving eigenvalues 1±t for every t in [0,1].
At t=1 both source frame operators equal I yet a mixed weaving has zero lower bound, also with a common identity fibre analysis map and swapped fusion subspaces.
integrity.proof_basis: Pointwise minimum and maximum of two equal-mass measurement-energy densities, exact interchange of joint infima and suprema, and diagonal 2-by-2 sharpness witnesses.
integrity.unproved_limits: The theorem-specific integrated-versus-pointwise positivity ambiguity is not resolved as an assertion about authorial intent.

limitations: The exact total-variation formulas assume two Parseval continuous g-fusion families with common measure-index set and measurable nonnegative local energy densities.

The theorem-specific reading of integrated positivity in the motivating source is ambiguous; the counterexample is conditional on the literal integrated-operator interpretation and does not refute pointwise local positivity.
No extension to non-Parseval systems, three or more simultaneous sources, or computable infinite-dimensional TV optimizers is asserted.

title: Exact total-variation weaving threshold for Parseval continuous \(g\)-fusion frames
